statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70197 (GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) is a remote code execution issue in System.Net.Sockets on Windows: reusing a SocketAsyncEventArgs instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can keep an undersized cached native address buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds write during ReceiveFromAsync. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows runtime packs (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64), affected before 10.0.14 and fixed in 10.0.14; the October 13 update did not carry the fix and the October 25 out-of-band update did (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/466, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/493, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md). The native address buffer that overflows is kept in SocketAsyncEventArgs.Windows.cs, which only the Windows build of System.Net.Sockets compiles (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/v10.0.114/src/runtime/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System.Net.Sockets.csproj). The fix (dotnet/dotnet commit b7fe82406537b588fdeda2ffcf73284ff83d59cb, in the v10.0.114 source tag and not in v10.0.113) sizes and grows that buffer correctly and also makes the shared Socket.cs replace an undersized cached SocketAddress; the Unix build passes the managed SocketAddress buffer, with its own length, to the receive call instead of a separately allocated native buffer (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/v10.0.113/src/runtime/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketAsyncEventArgs.Unix.cs). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: they ship the Linux (linux-musl) .NET shared framework and runtime packs, every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header, and none is a native Windows executable or DLL, so no Windows runtime pack is present. The Windows-only source file that holds the vulnerable buffer handling is therefore not compiled into the System.Net.Sockets assembly of any published build.

CVE-2026-70197 (GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) is a remote code execution issue in System.Net.Sockets on Windows: reusing a SocketAsyncEventArgs instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can keep an undersized cached native address buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds write during ReceiveFromAsync. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 8, only the Windows runtime packs (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64), affected before 8.0.33 and fixed in 8.0.33 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/466, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.33/8.0.33.md). System.Net.Sockets is built per platform: only the Windows build compiles SocketAsyncEventArgs.Windows.cs, which holds the cached native socket-address buffer that the fix changes, and the Unix build compiles SocketAsyncEventArgs.Unix.cs instead (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/v8.0.32/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System.Net.Sockets.csproj). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: they ship the Linux (linux-musl) .NET shared framework and runtime packs, every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header, none is a native Windows executable or DLL, and no Windows runtime pack is present. In each build and architecture, the System.Net.Sockets.dll implementation in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime is byte-identical to the copies in the .NET SDK and runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, which also holds a separate copy in its NativeAOT compiler pack; the other System.Net.Sockets.dll files are reference assemblies and small .NET Framework and .NET Standard facades with no socket code. In the shared-framework copy from every build on both architectures, and in the NativeAOT copy from the x86_64 8.0.32-r0 build, the metadata names the Unix members (TransferCompletionCallbackCore, ReceiveMessageFromCompletionCallback, _acceptedFileDescriptor) and none of the Windows members that manage that buffer (AllocateSocketAddressBuffer, PtrSocketAddressBuffer, _socketAddressPtr, DoOperationReceiveFromSingleBuffer, ProcessIOCPResult); the same search finds all of those Windows members in System.Net.Sockets.dll from Microsoft's win-x64 8.0.32 runtime pack. So the vulnerable Windows receive path is not compiled into the Linux builds this owner publishes.

CVE-2026-70197 (GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) is a remote code execution issue in System.Net.Sockets on Windows: reusing a SocketAsyncEventArgs instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can retain an undersized cached native address buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds write during ReceiveFromAsync. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Windows runtime packs (Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-*) as the affected packages; the .NET 9 fix shipped in 9.0.21 and was completed in 9.0.22 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/466, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135702, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md). System.Net.Sockets is built per platform: the Windows build compiles SocketAsyncEventArgs.Windows.cs, where the native address buffer is kept, and the Unix build compiles SocketAsyncEventArgs.Unix.cs instead (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/v9.0.22/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System.Net.Sockets.csproj). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every System.Net.Sockets.dll implementation in them is the Linux (linux-musl) build shipped in the .NET shared framework and the Linux runtime and ILCompiler packs; the other copies are reference assemblies or .NET Framework compatibility facades used by the SDK's build extensions, which hold no socket implementation. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file, so no Windows runtime pack is present. The Windows receive path that the fix changes is therefore not reached in any published build.
